clue.text: Addict, wrongly put in charge, is instructive

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters of the word addict are set out in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A drug user wrongly given authority somehow turns out to be educational.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' signals the anagram, and 'put' is only a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something meant to teach or lecture is didactic, so it is instructive.

clue.text: Some mice dearly like some cakes

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Mice are said to have a fondness for certain cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Many cakes are finished with a sugary topping, so they are covered in frosting like that.

parts.note: to pass on is a gentle way of saying someone dies
el is 'the' in Spanish, a foreign language

explanation.surface: Someone hands on the foreign fuel to another party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passes on' reads as handing over, but it means dies.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is the heavy oil burned in compression-ignition engines, a common fuel.

clue.text: Short time to grab dash of tanning pigment

indicators.note: to grab means the short time holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: min is the short form of minute, a time
dash in the sense of flair or verve is elan

explanation.surface: In a brief moment, someone snatches a bit of colour from a tan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dash of' looks like 'a little of' tanning, but dash is ELAN; 'of' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the dark pigment the skin produces in sunlight is what makes a suntan.

parts.note: to hand something over is to offer it
divers is an old word for various or several, i.e. some

explanation.surface: An offer made to scuba divers turns out to be bountiful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' is not underwater swimmers but the archaic adjective meaning several; 'find' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a large or liberal sum or reward is called a handsome one, meaning generous.

clue.text: Who keeps steward excited in novel?

indicators.note: keeps means the first word holds the rearranged letters inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: excited says the letters of steward are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A riddle about a character in some novel who has an agitated steward in custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who' looks like a question word but supplies its own letters, split round the anagram signalled by 'excited' and placed by 'keeps'. The title belongs to Charles Kingsley's 1855 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Charles Kingsley's 1855 adventure story of that title is a famous Victorian novel.

clue.text: Irish leader disposed of drug for operatic heroine

indicators.note: leader picks the opening letter of the word Irish

parts.note: goods disposed of in a sale have been sold
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An Irish chief got rid of a narcotic to benefit an opera's leading lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Irish princess in Wagner's Tristan und Isolde is a famous heroine of opera.

indicators.note: having means the first word contains the second within it

parts.note: to hate something is to dislike it
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone loathes having their friend Charlie come over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like Charlie visiting, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something flat and circular is shaped like a disc, i.e. round.

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: unwilling means disinclined or reluctant, i.e. averse

explanation.surface: Nations that are perpetually reluctant to act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' reads as countries, but it is a verb: declares.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to assert or declare something firmly is to aver it; one who does so asserts.

parts.note: an apprentice is a learner, L as on a learner driver's plate
and is a conjunction, a word that joins

explanation.surface: A trainee carpenter works in a shipyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joiner' suggests a carpenter, but it is the word AND, which joins clauses.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a ship that docks comes to land at the quay; to dock is to bring ashore.

clue.text: Stop and pay for laboratory apparatus …

parts.note: to stand someone a drink is to pay for it
a still is apparatus for distilling liquids

explanation.surface: Halt and cover the cost of some lab equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a complete halt, when all movement ceases, is a stop.

parts.note: twill is a woven fabric with diagonal ribs

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: picking whatever cloth one likes.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link this clue to the one before for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: doing something whenever or however one wishes is doing it freely, as one chooses.

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: upset says the letters of can are knocked into a new order

parts.note: a curate is an assistant clergyman

explanation.surface: A single tin can unsettle a vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something incorrect or mistaken is wrong.

clue.text: Devotee I get on with in time

parts.note: to get on with a task is to do it
in time means eventually, i.e. later

explanation.surface: A fan says they will get along with someone eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a worshipper of idols, or loosely an ardent admirer, is a devotee.

definitions.meaning: to withdraw a horse or competitor from a race
to tear at with nails or claws

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: withdrawing a runner from an event, and raking skin with nails.

indicators.note: during means the reversed piece sits inside the disagreement

parts.note: a clash is a disagreement

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a local is a pub, an inn

explanation.surface: A selective local person is upset in the middle of an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' is the British word for one's nearby pub, here INN; 'upset' reverses it to NNI.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a clique that excludes outsiders is discriminative in its loyalties.

indicators.note: absorbing means the first word takes the second into itself

parts.note: pent, as in pent up, means confined
a dan is a judoka's grade of black belt

explanation.surface: Someone shut away after taking in a judo fighter's execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link here. 'hanging' suggests execution but is a noun: an ornament that hangs.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a jewel hanging on a chain round the neck is a hanging ornament.

indicators.note: aspiration is the breathy h sound, so the letter H is dropped

parts.note: equestrians are riders, horsemen

explanation.surface: Nordic people call riders unambitious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' looks like ambition, but it is the phonetic term for an H sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the early inhabitants of Norway and Scandinavia, especially the Vikings.

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: results are outcomes, ends

explanation.surface: Sentries are sick of the outcomes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed up' reads as fed up, but 'up' reverses FED to DEF; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to guard something is to protect it from attack.

parts.note: a lock is a second-row forward in rugby
a lifetime is an age

explanation.surface: A British rugby forward's whole career has been one long hindrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something that jams a pipe or route is an obstruction.

indicators.note: settlement suggests the letters of Ulster being settled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The glory of a colonial settlement in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement' recalls the Plantation of Ulster, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative synonym: brilliance or distinction that brings honour, i.e. glory.

clue.text: Scottish leaders make claim of property in searches

parts.note: the leading letters, the first two, of Scottish
saying it is ours is a claim of property

explanation.surface: Scotland's chiefs stake a claim to land during their hunts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' is plural, taking the first two letters of Scottish; 'make' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one who scours an area searches it thoroughly.

definitions.meaning: to start something going, such as a chain of events
to show to advantage, as a frame does a picture

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: triggering an event, and enhancing something by contrast.

indicators.note: out means the letters of sent rating are put out of order

explanation.surface: A sailor sent off for a drink of bitter beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rating' is a naval sailor and 'bitter' a British beer, but the definition is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sharp, harsh taste or remark is bitter, puckering or caustic.

indicators.note: touring means the people go all round the next piece

parts.note: people are men
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Seeking people travelling around Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a person's bearing or expression is their look.

parts.note: any one means any

explanation.surface: Plenty of people are married, or at least one is.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a great number, lots, is many.

clue.text: Speaks, when scratching head, of taxes

indicators.note: scratching head means the first letter is struck off

parts.note: one who orates speaks formally

explanation.surface: Someone talks, rubbing their head, about taxation.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: local property taxes in Britain were called rates.

clue.text: Supporter is to give way about finale

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to give way to someone is to defer to them
a finale is the end

explanation.surface: A fan must yield over a final match.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one who stands up for a cause or person is a supporter.
